stem: Two flat mirrors are parallel, as shown. A light beam strikes the lower mirror at point \(P\), making a \(35^{\circ}\) angle with the mirror, and reflects to point \(Q\) on the upper mirror. There it reflects again and strikes the lower mirror at point \(R\). At each mirror the beam makes equal angles with the mirror before and after reflecting. What is the value of \(x\), the measure of angle \(PQR\)?
solution: After reflecting at \(P\), the beam \(\overline{PQ}\) makes a \(35^{\circ}\) angle with the lower mirror.

The mirrors are parallel and \(\overline{PQ}\) is a transversal, so \(\overline{PQ}\) also makes a \(35^{\circ}\) angle with the upper mirror (alternate interior angles). By the reflection rule, \(\overline{QR}\) makes a \(35^{\circ}\) angle with the upper mirror too.
The two \(35^{\circ}\) angles and angle \(PQR\) form a straight angle at \(Q\): \(x = 180 - 35 - 35 = 110\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. 35 is the angle each beam makes with the upper mirror, not the angle between the two beams.
explanation.B: Correct. At \(Q\) the beams make \(35^{\circ}\) angles with the mirror on each side, so \(x = 180 - 70 = 110\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. \(70\) is the sum of the two \(35^{\circ}\) angles at \(Q\); angle \(PQR\) is what remains of the straight angle, \(180 - 70\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is \(180 - 35\); both beams at \(Q\) make \(35^{\circ}\) angles with the mirror, so \(35\) must be subtracted twice.

verify:
P=figure['points']
d=lambda a,b: sqrt((P[a][0]-P[b][0])**2+(P[a][1]-P[b][1])**2)
ang=lambda a,v,b: N(acos(((P[a][0]-P[v][0])*(P[b][0]-P[v][0])+(P[a][1]-P[v][1])*(P[b][1]-P[v][1]))/(d(a,v)*d(b,v)))*180/pi)
assert P['M1'][1]==P['M2'][1]==P['P'][1]==P['R'][1] and P['N1'][1]==P['N2'][1]==P['Q'][1]
assert abs(ang('Q','P','R')-35)<0.1 and abs(ang('S','P','M1')-35)<0.1
assert abs(ang('P','Q','N1')-ang('R','Q','N2'))<0.1
ans=180-2*35
assert abs(ang('P','Q','R')-ans)<0.1
assert value(choices[answer])==ans==110
assert all(value(choices[k])!=ans for k in choices if k!=answer)
